newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber ends steady on modest buying.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber ends steady on modest buying.

text.p: Rubber futures closed steady on Monday largely on the back of modest shortcovering for RSS3 rubber, but volumes remain thin and the market may drift in the absence of fresh incentives, dealers said.

"There was a small amount of shortcovering for RSS3 rubber done by local dealers. But there were no trades done for RSS1 or TSR20 rubber. The market is very quiet and it will likely drift sideways the rest of the week," a local rubber trader said.
"Prices were also boosted by firm Japanese prices. This enabled the market to hold at their present levels," another dealer said.

Tokyo's benchmark May contract climbed 1.3 yen to 147.3 while Kobe's May contract was 0.1 yen up at 146.8. Almost 3,000 tonnes of the January RSS3 contract was traded in the local market. Some 900 tonnes of the April/June contract was traded.
At around 0945 GMT, January RSS3 was seen at 124.00-125.00 U.S. cents a kg compared with the previous 124.00 cents.
February RSS1 was indicated at 179.50-181.50 Singapore cents (US$1.28-$1.30) a kg against 180.50 cents.
February TSR20 was indicated at 173.00-175.00 Singapore cents (US$1.23-$1.25) a kg from 174.00 cents.
